# Troubleshooting quick reference

Error message / symptom → likely cause → fix. Ordered roughly by where in the workflow you'll hit them.

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `400 Required field 'PrimaryAttribute' is missing` (creating a table) | Tried to set `PrimaryNameAttribute` as a top-level string | Set `IsPrimaryName: true` directly on the primary attribute object instead. See [dataverse-web-api.md](dataverse-web-api.md) |
| `400 key ... not valid for resource RelationshipMetadataBase` | Addressed a relationship by `LogicalName` | Relationships must be addressed by `MetadataId` GUID — filter by `SchemaName` first to get the GUID |
| `0x8004f01f ... referenced by 1 other components` (deleting a table) | AppModule and/or Code App still reference the table as a component/data source | Remove AppModule components → republish → remove Code App data source → rebuild+redeploy Code App → delete relationships → delete table. See [model-driven-app.md](model-driven-app.md) |
| `400 query parameters not supported on complex type` (on `.../Privileges`) | Tried `$select` on an entity's `Privileges` navigation | Don't use `$select` here — request the full response and filter client-side |
| `400 Cannot read the value '3' as a quoted JSON string value` (AddPrivilegesRole) | Sent `Depth` as an integer | `Depth` must be the string `"Basic"`/`"Local"`/`"Deep"`/`"Global"` |
| `405 Operation not supported on EntityMetadata` (updating `IsAuditEnabled` or similar) | Used PATCH | Use PUT against `EntityDefinitions(<guid>)/IsAuditEnabled` with the full `@odata.type` annotation |
| `400 Invalid property 'metadataid' ... on type 'Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.entity'` (AddAppComponents) | Used `metadataid` as the bind key | Use `entityid` for table components on an AppModule |
| `404 Resource not found for the segment 'Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.AddAppComponents'` | Called it as a bound action (`appmodules(<guid>)/...AddAppComponents`) | It's unbound: `POST /AddAppComponents` with `{AppId, Components}` in the body. See [model-driven-app.md](model-driven-app.md) |
| `400 An undeclared property 'appmodulesitemap_association' which only has property annotations...` | Tried to link a sitemap to an AppModule via a nav-property PATCH | That property doesn't exist — add the sitemap via `AddAppComponents` instead (`@odata.type: Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.sitemap`), same as tables |
| `400 An ODataPrimitiveValue was instantiated with a value of type 'ODataEntityReferenceLink'...` (AddAppComponents) | Used `entityid@odata.bind` / `sitemapid@odata.bind` inside a `Components` array item | These are plain `Edm.Guid` properties on the polymorphic component item, not navigable — fetch the real GUID and set it as a literal value, not a bind |
| `400 The ID ... doesn't exist or isn't valid for the component type "SiteMap"` | Used `sitemapidunique` (the URL-addressing GUID) instead of `sitemapid` (the true metadata PK) in an `AddAppComponents` component | Sitemaps have two different GUIDs — fetch both (`$select=sitemapid,sitemapidunique`) and use `sitemapid` for component references |
| `400 Attribute 'webresourceid' cannot be NULL` (creating an `appmodule`) | Omitted or nulled `webresourceid` | It's required (the app's tile icon) and a plain `Edm.Guid`, not a lookup — set any valid web resource GUID directly, no `@odata.bind` |
| App shows "This app is designed for the legacy web client..." warning banner | `clienttype` wasn't set at AppModule creation, defaulting to `2` (legacy) | Always set `clienttype: 4` (Unified Interface) explicitly — every correctly configured app, including Microsoft's own, uses `4` |
| `404 Resource not found for the segment 'Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.ValidateApp'` | `ValidateApp` isn't exposed as a callable Web API action in at least some Dataverse versions | Skip it — it's optional (warnings/lint only) and not required for the app to work; just publish |
| `400 Error in parsing formxml. Line 1. Position N ... error occurred while parsing EntityName` | Unescaped `&` (or `<`/`>`/`"`) in a FormXml label/description string | XML-escape all label text before interpolating into FormXml — the position points at the bad character but the message doesn't say so |
| Sitemap groups show as `Unknown0` / `Unknown1` | `Title LCID` doesn't match the org's base language | `GET /organizations?$select=languagecode` and match every `Title LCID` to it |
| `Entity 'appmodule' with Id=... Does Not Exist` right after creating an AppModule | Misleading error — usually really `DuplicateAppModuleUniqueName`; the record was created but your lookup only checked published apps | Also query `POST /appmodules/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.RetrieveUnpublishedMultiple` |
| `403 CodeAppOperationNotAllowedInEnvironment` (on `power-apps push`) | "Enable code apps" feature not turned on for the environment | Enable it in Power Platform Admin Center → Environments → Settings; wait a few minutes for propagation |
| `power-apps init` fails: "power.config.json already exists" | Project already scaffolded | Skip `init`; edit `power.config.json` fields directly (e.g. `environmentId`) |
| SDK runtime error after upgrading `@microsoft/power-apps` (e.g. missing `initialize` export) | Upgraded the SDK past what the app code was written against | Pin the SDK to the version the app was built with; add `@microsoft/power-apps-cli` as a separate devDependency instead of upgrading the SDK |
| Image/logo renders in local dev but is a broken image after `power-apps push` | File lives in `public/` and is referenced by string path, not bundled | Move to `src/assets/` and `import` it as an ES module. See [code-app-deployment.md](code-app-deployment.md) |
| `delete-data-source` deletes generated files for tables you wanted to KEEP | CLI bug in some versions — wipes all legacy-style `models`/`services` files, not just the target table's | Restore the wiped files for kept tables from a pristine backup/export; check for dangling field/import references (e.g. a lookup pointing at the now-deleted table) |
| Exported managed solution "works" in dev but a Code App is missing from the package | Code App component was created in the environment's Default Solution, not your named solution | `POST /AddSolutionComponent` with `ComponentType: 300` and your `SolutionUniqueName`; verify via `solutioncomponents` |
| `401` mid-script | Azure CLI access token expired (typically ~1 hour) | Re-run `az account get-access-token` and retry; write scripts to refresh the token automatically on 401 rather than failing |
| `400 0x8006088a "The 'startswith' function isn't supported for Metadata Entities"` (listing tables) | Tried `$filter=startswith(LogicalName,'ctso_')` on `EntityDefinitions` | No server-side prefix filter exists for metadata — fetch with `$filter=IsCustomEntity eq true` and filter by prefix client-side. See [dataverse-web-api.md](dataverse-web-api.md) |
| `RelationshipDefinitions?$filter=ReferencingEntity eq '...'` returns `200` with an empty array | Missing the `/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.OneToManyRelationshipMetadata` type-cast segment — `ReferencingEntity` doesn't exist on the base type, so the filter silently matches nothing instead of erroring | Always query `RelationshipDefinitions/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.OneToManyRelationshipMetadata?$filter=ReferencingEntity eq '...'`. See [dataverse-web-api.md](dataverse-web-api.md) |
| `RetrieveUserContext: SecLib::CheckPrivilege failed` for a specific user (app works fine for you) | Your test account is a System Administrator (bypasses privilege checks); the failing user's role(s) lack core-platform privileges (`usersettings`, `businessunit`, `team`, `organization`) that a script-built role never gets by default | Copy the relevant privileges from the OOB `Basic User` role onto your custom role. See [security-and-audit.md](security-and-audit.md) |
| A required field (`ApplicationRequired`) still gets saved blank | The field isn't actually on the form the user is looking at, or a published form change hasn't reached an already-open session | Verify the field's `datafieldname` is in the live `formxml` for every form/app that touches this table; have the user hard-refresh/reopen the app. See [dataverse-web-api.md §10](dataverse-web-api.md#10-requiredlevel-is-enforced-client-side-and-only-for-fields-actually-on-the-form) |
| A form field that should be user-editable is always auto-populated / never shows the value you set | The control is bound (`datafieldname`) to a standard system field (`ownerid`, `createdby`) that looks similar to your custom field, not your custom field itself | Check the form's `datafieldname` against your schema's actual logical name. See [model-driven-app.md](model-driven-app.md) |
| App/table works for the app you're testing but a *different* app that reads the same table crashes with a null-reference error after you added a second app | Multiple apps share a table; a constraint (RequiredLevel, an async flow) that looked sufficient for the writer doesn't actually prevent the reader from seeing a null | Add null-guards (optional chaining + fallback) in the reading app for every field sourced from a relationship — don't rely solely on writer-side constraints. See [multi-app-data-integrity.md](multi-app-data-integrity.md) |
| `add-data-source` for a connector 404s with a mangled URL | Git Bash/MSYS rewrites any CLI arg starting with `/` into a Windows path | Pass the short `apiId` (e.g. `shared_microsoftcopilotstudio`), not the full `/providers/...` path. See [connector-data-sources.md](connector-data-sources.md) |
| `Data source not found: <connectorKey>` at runtime, even though `add-data-source` succeeded and the connection shows "Connected" in the Maker Portal | Client-side singleton race: the app's older Dataverse-only data-source-info generator seeds `PowerDataSourcesInfoProvider` before the connector's own generated service gets a chance to, and the singleton then ignores every later, more-complete call | Merge Connector-type entries from `.power/schemas/appschemas/dataSourcesInfo.ts` into the older generator's output. See [connector-data-sources.md](connector-data-sources.md) |
| `400 "Invalid request body"` / "The response is not in a JSON format." calling `ExecuteCopilotAsyncV2` (Copilot Studio connector) | Missing `notificationUrl` in the request body — required by the connector gateway even for synchronous use, despite the generated TS signature not marking it required | Always pass a `notificationUrl` (a placeholder string is fine if you don't need the callback). See [connector-data-sources.md](connector-data-sources.md) |
| A field that looks like it should auto-increment (`...Number`, primary-name attribute) never gets populated automatically, and stays blank if the user doesn't type something | It's a plain `String` attribute (`AutoNumberFormat: null`), not Dataverse's native AutoNumber type, despite the display name suggesting otherwise | Check `AutoNumberFormat` on the attribute via `EntityDefinitions(...)/Attributes` before assuming it self-populates; if it isn't a real autonumber, either set it client-side on create or add a post-create Power Automate flow that fills it when empty |

## General debugging approach

1. Read the full Dataverse error response body, not just the HTTP status — it usually names the exact field/property that's wrong.
2. When an error message seems inconsistent with what you did (e.g. "entity does not exist" right after you just created it), consider that it may be a **misleading wrapper around a different underlying error** — check for duplicate-name conflicts, unpublished-state visibility gaps, or eventual-consistency delays before assuming your create request failed outright.
3. When in doubt about a Web API resource's exact key/property names, fetch `<environmentUrl>/api/data/v9.2/$metadata` and search it directly — it's the ground truth for every entity type, key, and bound action shape.
